Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare the internal RFP packet, the security and ops teams asked for a concise evidentiary response to several private-deploy questions. We would appreciate a single-threaded response we can attach to the vendor assessment. Our immediate asks: 

1) Installation/network: required inbound/outbound ports, default FQDNs, and an example network diagram for a VPC + NATed air-gapped scenario.
2) Cryptography: native KMS integration, HSM support, key rotation practices, whether customer-owned keys are supported for data at rest and for TLS certs.
3) Updates: offline patch process for air-gapped installs, expected maintenance window duration, rollback strategy, and signed package verification.
4) Audit & evidence: log retention defaults (tokens, admin actions), ability to stream to customer's SIEM, and SOC2/ISO artifacts available.
5) Support & SLA: recommended support coverage for private installs, on-call handoff, and target time-to-first-response for critical incidents.

If you can bundle answers and any diagrams/docs in one email that would be ideal — procurement wants a single ZIP to attach to the bid file. Also share an approximate lead time for a customer-managed on-prem kickoff (e.g., prep through readiness).

Thanks — Emily

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Answers below in the body and attached are our supporting artifacts (install guide, network diagram, HSM notes, patch-summary). I kept bullets short for your RFP slot.

1) Installation / network
- Required outbound: TCP 443 to Redwood control plane (customer can opt for private control-plane proxy; see section 2.1 of the install guide).
- Inbound: none required for normal inference; optional access for admin UI (allowlist by IP/RBAC).
- For air-gapped installs we provide a pull-based update bundle and an ops-only bastion pattern in the diagram. See attachment: network_diagram_portaledge_v2.png.

2) Cryptography
- Customer-managed KMS: supported via AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, GCP KMS, and PKCS#11 HSMs.
- HSM support: validated integrations for HSM-backed key wrapping (sample connector included).
- Key rotation: we support policy-driven rotation; we provide tooling for re-wrapping model keys with zero-downtime rekey where supported.
- TLS: customer can supply certs (SNI) or we can use locally-issued certs; mutual TLS available for peer services.

3) Updates (air-gapped)
- Mechanism: signed bundle exported from control plane; customer imports via UI/CLI.
- Patch cadence: security patches as-needed, minor releases quarterly, major releases with 60d notice.
- Rollback: each bundle includes a rollback manifest; we support automatic fallback to last-known-good for runtime.
- Verification: bundles are signed with our PKI; signature verified during import.

4) Audit & evidence
- Logs: admin actions and sys events default 90d retention; tokenized usage logs 30d by default (configurable).
- SIEM: can push via syslog/CEF or export S3-compatible buckets for ingestion.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 scope doc — we provide an evidence packet under NDA.

5) Support & SLA
- Recommended: Dedicated Engineering Oncall during onboarding + Bronze/L2 retained SLA for production (options documented in the contract addendum).
- Response: P1 (security incident) — 1 hour acknowledgement, 4 hour initial triage target. Custom SLAs available as part of Dedicated contracts.

Lead time: typical customer-managed on-prem kickoff (pre-reqs met) = 3–4 weeks. For air-gapped/regulated customers allow additional 2–3 weeks for secure network validation.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_installation_guide_v1.3.pdf; network_diagram_portaledge_v2.png; hsm_kms_integration_notes.docx; airgap_patch_process_summary.pdf

Would you like a single ZIP for procurement, or separate files for security/ops? We can generate a signed bundle and a short one-page evidence summary if that helps.

—Naomi

Emily — answers inline below. Forwarding a short SOW template we use internally (snippet included).

> On the control-plane proxy and telemetry
You can run a private control-plane proxy in your VPC. Outbound requirements then reduce to a single egress to our artifact repository for signed bundles (artifact.redwood-inference.com:443). If you require zero egress, we support a fully air-gapped workflow (manual export/import over secure media). I'll attach an explicit host allowlist in the ZIP.

> Key rotation and live inference impact
Rotation for model-wrapping keys is designed to be non-disruptive: the runtime re-wraps the envelope keys while maintaining the KV cache. For extremely long-running single-token streams there can be a micro-window (<1s) for key swap acknowledgment; plan-based tests showed no user-facing latency beyond typical jitter. We recommend scheduling rotation during low-traffic windows for peace-of-mind.

> Events schema for SIEM mapping
Embedding a sample events.json schema in the ZIP. Fields include: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_id, model_id, prompt_hash (tokenized), bytes_in, bytes_out.

2) Provisioning: VM/GPU sizing, storage, networking, HSM/KMS integration checks (16–24 hrs).
3) Installation: control-plane proxy setup, runtime install, model seeding, smoke tests (24–32 hrs).
4) Hardening & validation: cert installs, RBAC, SIEM forward, backup verification (8–16 hrs).
5) Handover & runbook: runbook walkthrough, runbook delivery, run-of-show for failover testing (8–12 hrs).
6) Post-go-live support: 2 weeks hypercare with 2 engineer-days/week (est. 16 hrs).

Estimate ranges by complexity (baseline 8–12 person-days; air-gapped / enterprise add 6–10 additional person-days).
